title: Flow Cytometry Trait Measurements of Diatoms
author: Phoebe Argyle
materials: Aliquot 200 µL of live, uniform culture and transfer to a round-bottom tissue culture plate. Agitate culture gently to suspend cells to create a uniform culture. 96 Well TC-Treated Microplates (Microplate, Corning®, CLS3799-1EA, https://www.sigmaaldrich.com )

The multi-spectra beads CytoFlex Daily QC Beads Beckman Coulter Catalog #B53230 that are used to calibrate the instrument on startup may also be used to ensure comparability between experimental runs. It is recommended to analyse samples from one experiment on the same day, however if this is not possible it is necessary to ensure that the instrument is performing similarly on the different days of analysis. Using the parameters and thresholds established for diatoms, the QC beads may be run as if they were a sample and gated according to their chlorophyll fluorescence, forward scatter and side scatter (see image below). This way, if the beads fall within the same gates on each day of analysis, it may be assumed that samples run on different days may be fairly compared. Daily QC beads gated according to forward scatter (FSC-A) and side scatter (SSC-A) In addition to the QC beads, beads of known diameter were used to create a linear calibration of forward scatter vs. spherical size. For this protocol, beads of 2,4,6,10 and 15µm Flow Cytometry Size Calibration Kit (nonfluorescent microspheres) Thermo Fisher Catalog #F13838 were used. These beads can also be used to ensure the performance of the instrument is consistent across experimental runs for FSC and SSC measures (see image).

steps.title: Run daily instrument quality control
steps.instruction: Perform the CytoFLEX LX daily QC using the multi‑spectra beads to verify instrument performance before any sample analysis.

substeps.instruction: Obtain CytoFlex Daily QC Beads (Beckman Coulter Catalog #B53230).
Run the QC protocol exactly as described in the CytoFLEX LX user manual.

steps.title: Fix diatom cells with paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Add paraformaldehyde to achieve a final concentration of 0.8 % (v/v) and handle the reagent in a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL of 8 % (EM‑Grade, Emgrid Catalog #157‑8, CAS 30525‑89‑4) paraformaldehyde to each sample, which is 10 % of the total sample volume.
Mix gently to obtain a final paraformaldehyde concentration of 0.8 % (v/v).
Carry out the addition inside a fume hood because paraformaldehyde is toxic.

steps.title: Seal plate and store refrigerated
steps.instruction: Prevent evaporation of fixed samples and keep them cold until analysis.

substeps.instruction: Secure the plate lid tightly.
Wrap the plate edges with Parafilm (Parafilm M, PM996; available from many vendors).
Store the sealed plate at 4 °C.
Analyze the samples within 48 h, preferably on the same day they were fixed.

steps.title: Load plate into the flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Place the prepared plate into the CytoFLEX LX instrument for acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Insert the plate into the CytoFLEX LX flow cytometer (Beckman Coulter, C40312, 21 detectors, 6 lasers).

steps.title: Optimize detector gain and thresholds
steps.instruction: Set appropriate gain and threshold values for the detectors that will be used to discriminate diatom cells from background.

substeps.instruction: Use a spare aliquot of diatom culture or filtered culture media (0.22 µm filter) to establish background scatter.
Forward Scatter Area (FSC‑A): Si‑photodiode with built‑in 488/8 nm band‑pass filter; set threshold to 4000.
Side Scatter Area (SSC‑A): 488 nm laser, 50 mW, optical filter 488/8 nm.
Chlorophyll‑a (B690‑50): 488 nm laser, 50 mW, optical filter 690/50 nm; set threshold to 2000.
Adjust gain for each detector as needed to obtain clear separation of the diatom population.

steps.title: Mix samples and acquire data
steps.instruction: Run each sample through the cytometer, ensuring adequate mixing, flow rate, and event collection.

substeps.instruction: Mix each well for 6 seconds using the CytoFLEX mixing function before acquisition.
Run the sample at a medium flow rate of 30 µL min⁻¹ for 1 minute (00:01:00).
Collect a minimum of 200 events per sample; aim for ≥2000 events for higher precision.
Confirm that the abort rate remains <1 %; if the culture is very dense, reduce the flow rate, and if very dilute, increase the flow rate or extend acquisition time.
Gate diatom cells visually on a plot of chlorophyll‑a fluorescence (B690‑50) versus FSC‑A to exclude debris and non‑cellular particles.

steps.title: Calculate equivalent spherical diameter
steps.instruction: Derive cell size from FSC using a calibration curve based on size beads.

substeps.instruction: Measure FSC values for calibration beads of known diameters.
Create a linear equation linking FSC to bead diameter; example: Spherical size = (FSC + 275,549) / 83,539.
Apply this equation to the median FSC value of the diatom population (median calculated from ≥200 cells) to obtain the equivalent spherical diameter (ESD).

steps.title: Determine granularity and chlorophyll‑a metrics
steps.instruction: Extract relative fluorescence units for side‑scatter and chlorophyll‑a and optionally normalise them to cell size.

substeps.instruction: Obtain the median side‑scatter (SSC‑A) and chlorophyll‑a (B690‑50) values from ≥200 cells; report them in relative fluorescence units (RFU).
For comparative analyses, correct these median RFU values against the calculated ESD, because granularity and chlorophyll‑a are correlated with cell size.
